title: Taxonomic Documentation Under Uncertainty: Data Quality and Provenance in a Pirabas Formation Fossil Collection from the Brazilian Amazon
content: The Pirabas Formation preserves an abundant and diverse Miocene marine-to-estuarine fossil record in northern Brazil, but the research value of ex situ material depends on taxonomic and provenance data that can be traced and revised. This study evaluates taxonomic documentation and data quality in the Natural Heritage Collection (Coleção de Patrimônio Natural, CPAN) of the Federal University of Pará, which is housed in a Museology Program rather than a biological, geological, or paleontological unit. Institutional records, the cataloguing workflow, published sources, and an audit of 106 paleontological inventory records dated 2 September 2026 were examined. The scientific-name field was populated in 105 records (99.1%) and the phylum field in 104 (98.1%), whereas collector, collection date, acquisition date, origin, and acquisition mode were absent from all 106 records in the audited spreadsheet. Only 28 entries (26.4%) used genus-level or genus-style nomenclature, 45 (42.5%) contained formal suprageneric taxa, 32 (30.2%) used descriptive, vernacular, or material-based labels, and one record was blank. At least 12 records contained direct contradictions between populated broad taxonomic fields. Identifier review also detected one duplicated current registration code and one duplicated previous number. A seven-stage protocol was operationally applied to representative documentary cases without re-examining or reidentifying specimens. The metadata elements proposed in the protocol were compared with relevant Darwin Core terms to assess their potential for interoperability. The results show that high nominal completion of taxonomic fields does not necessarily indicate taxonomic precision or documentary reliability. Treating uncertainty, provenance gaps, and revision history as explicit data strengthens traceability and future research usability while keeping documentary quality control distinct from specialist taxonomic validation.
